title: introduce-local-fastpath-and-staged-ci-lanes-to-speed-feedback
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Add a lightweight 'local-fastpath' CI workflow and supporting developer tooling to reduce turn-around for common developer edits. Split heavy integration suites into staged CI lanes (fast/unit -> gated/integration -> nightly/regression) and introduce a small 'deps-steward' diagnostic job that surfaces non-critical but actionable dependency drift. Motivation: developer feedback loops are currently dominated by a monolithic CI that runs expensive integration tests for many PRs. This causes slower iteration, noisy reruns, and discourages small, frequent changes. Goals: 1) Provide a fast green path for lint + unit tests that runs on push and PR comment triggers; 2) Stage long-running tests behind explicit gates and schedule full suites nightly; 3) Improve contributor on-boarding with a fast-init helper that caches common toolchains and bootstraps repo state locally; 4) Surface dependency issues without automatically bumping (diagnostic only). Implementation highlights: - Add .github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml: a compact workflow that runs only changed-package unit tests, lint, and typecheck with optional --changed-files detection. It runs on push, pull_request, and workflow_dispatch. - Add .github/workflows/ci-staged-gates.yml: creates a three-lane pipeline. The fast lane (always run) -> gated integration lane (manual/canary on approvals) -> regression/nightly lane (cron). Gate transitions are implemented with artifacts and a small signaling file to keep job dependencies lightweight. - New scripts/fast-init.ts: a node-based bootstrap that caches toolchain artifacts (pnpm store snapshot, prebuilt hermetic binaries) and provides a single-step local dev sync. - tools/deps-steward/*: lightweight action that runs 'pnpm audit', 'npm outdated --json' and evaluates against our internal dep policy (max-minor drift). It uploads a report to PR checks and adds a comment summarizing noteworthy drift; it does NOT auto-create PRs. - ci/helpers/changed-packages.sh: improved changed-package detection to avoid running full monorepo tests for small packages. - package.json / pnpm-workspace.yaml: minor workspace rearrangement to make changed-package detection more accurate. - Update docs/developer/README.md: document fast-init usage and the staged CI expectations. Rollout plan: 1) Merge in feature-flagged mode (env CI_FASTPATH=enabled for main runners). 2) Monitor flakes and coverage of changed-package detection for two weeks. 3) If signal is good, flip default and move heavy integration to manual/canary or nightly only. Manual testing performed: local runs, CI dry-runs on a test branch, and dogfood usage by a small eng subset. Checklist:
- [x] Add fastpath workflow and changed-package detector
- [x] Add fast-init bootstrap script with basic caching
- [x] Add staged gates workflow with artifact handoff
- [x] Add deps-steward diagnostics (no autopromote)
- [x] Document dev workflow and update contributor guide
- [x] Smoke test across macOS/Linux self-hosted runners Known limitations and follow-ups: - The changed-package detector currently uses git diff heuristics and may under-estimate when codegen artifacts are touched; follow-up ENG-902 will add finer-grained file-to-target mapping. - Deps-steward reports are advisory; future work (ENG-913) will propose automatic minor bump PRs for low-risk packages. - Fast-init currently caches pnpm store and node-prebuilds; we will iterate to support containerized local dev next.

c3b9a2f: feat(scripts): introduce fast-init.ts bootstrap and cache layer
d4e55b1: infra: staged CI lanes with artifact handoff and gating
b6f40d0: tools: add deps-steward diagnostics and PR report formatter

review_comments: Evan Cho: This looks promising. Can you add a small benchmark for median CI latency improvement with a sample of 50 PRs?
Priya Kapoor: Added a metrics dashboard artifact and a short run summary to docs/notes. See ci/metrics/fastpath-dashboard.json.
María Torres: The gating handoff uses a temporary artifact file — can we avoid storing large artifacts in the runner? Suggest we use a 1KB signal file and put real logs in object storage.
Priya Kapoor: Switched to a 1KB signal approach and upload logs to s3-compatible artifact store in the staged gate implementation (second commit).
Liam O'Neill: deps-steward output is useful but noisy; can we add a severity filter so PRs only get a comment when a package is > minor out-of-date?
Priya Kapoor: Toggled severity threshold to 'minor+' by default; added per-PR opt-out via deps-steward:skip label.
María Torres: Please confirm fast-init doesn't leak credentials when caching.
ci_checks: unit-tests (fastpath): failed on first run (flake in test-utils), rerun passed
integration (gated): skipped on PR (staged gate) — will run manually for initial rollouts
deps-steward: report uploaded to PR checks (severity minor+), no auto-bumps
release_notes: Introduce a compact CI fastpath for lint and unit-tests, staged CI lanes to reduce noise from long-running integrations, a fast-init local bootstrap for faster on-boarding, and a non-invasive dependency diagnostic (deps-steward). Expected result: ~3x faster green feedback for small PRs and fewer full-suite runs in main CI.
